procedimientos.endoscopia.desc.1: In general, endoscopic sinus surgery is aimed at people with chronic sinusitis problems that do not respond to medical treatment.
procedimientos.endoscopia.sintomas.lista: Facial pain or feeling of heaviness., Difficulty breathing through the nose., Persistent bad smell in the nose., Postnasal drip., Headaches.
procedimientos.endoscopia.desc.2: Occasionally sinus problems can cause hoarseness, cough, general malaise, or a variety of other symptoms; but these problems can also occur in the absence of sinus disease; therefore, the diagnosis of sinusitis should be based on a meticulous evaluation by your doctor.
procedimientos.endoscopia.desc.3: In most people with sinus problems, surgery is not indicated. In most cases they are successfully resolved with medical treatment. This treatment may consist of antibiotics, anti-inflammatories, antihistamines, decongestants or other medications, treatment for allergies, or environmental control (e.g., quitting smoking).
procedimientos.endoscopia.desc.4: When there is no longer a response to medical treatments, an endoscopic surgical procedure should be performed.
procedimientos.endoscopia.desc.5: Before indicating endoscopic sinus surgery, radiological studies (CT scan) should be performed to determine which areas are affected and initiate a surgical plan to cure the disease.
procedimientos.endoscopia.seguimiento.ti: Evaluation and Follow-up of Endoscopic Treatment
procedimientos.endoscopia.cirugia.desc.1: If, after consultation, it is considered that you would benefit from endoscopic surgery, a date will be arranged for the procedure. In many cases, surgery can be performed on an outpatient basis; however, it is important to be prepared to be admitted to the hospital if necessary.
procedimientos.endoscopia.cirugia.desc.2: After surgery, follow-up visits are necessary for approximately three weeks to clean scabs from the surgical site. An additional visit is scheduled later between two to six weeks.
procedimientos.endoscopia.cirugia.desc.3: In some cases, a second surgical procedure may be necessary if symptoms reappear after an interval of relief, usually due to the formation of adhesions (scar tissue).
procedimientos.endoscopia.tecnica.desc.1: This surgery differs from the conventional surgical approach, as it is performed using a camera (endoscopes) through the nostrils, without any external cuts and without a scalpel.
procedimientos.endoscopia.tecnica.desc.2: The principle is to increase the drainage of the cavities that accumulate mucus and become infected; frequently the anterior ethmoidal, maxillary, and frontal areas.
procedimientos.endoscopia.tecnica.desc.3: If the underlying cause of the disease is identified and corrected, secondary disease in the maxillary and frontal sinuses often improves spontaneously.
procedimientos.endoscopia.ventajas.exito: Results have been very successful, with over 90% cure rate.
procedimientos.endoscopia.que-es.desc: Sinusitis is a very common condition that requires the attention of a nose specialist, such as Dr. Lumbán. If you have questions about this condition and its symptoms, click on View More Information.
procedimientos.antirronquido.desc.1: Snoring can affect sleep quality and overall health. In many cases it is associated with upper airway obstruction, soft palate vibration, or increased pharyngeal tissue.
procedimientos.antirronquido.desc.2: When snoring is persistent or accompanied by breathing pauses, it is important to perform a complete evaluation to rule out sleep apnea and define the appropriate treatment.
procedimientos.antirronquido.diagnostico: Dr. Lumbán performs a comprehensive evaluation of the upper airway, including medical history, physical examination, and specialized studies such as nasofibroscopy.
In some cases, a polysomnography is requested to measure sleep quality and quantify the presence of obstructive apnea.
procedimientos.antirronquido.conservador: Avoid alcohol and sedatives at night
Treatment of allergies and nasal congestion
Management is individualized according to the patient's anatomy and the severity of symptoms.
procedimientos.antirronquido.procedimien: Anti-snoring surgery is planned based on the area of greatest obstruction. The objective is to widen the airway and decrease tissue vibration.
Depending on the case, the procedure can be outpatient with controlled recovery.
procedimientos.antirronquido.recuperacio: Relative rest during the first week
Control of discomfort with indicated medication
procedimientos.antirronquido.cta.desc: You can contact Dr. Lumbán by phone, email, or schedule an appointment to resolve all your questions.
procedimientos.laringe.desc.1: Hoarseness (dysphonia) or change in the sound of the voice is a common symptom. It is often related to inflammation from overuse of the voice or temperature changes, and usually resolves spontaneously in less than 3 weeks.
procedimientos.laringe.desc.2: In some cases, voice changes may be the first symptom of a more serious condition such as vocal weakness, vocal cord tumors, or even throat cancer. If hoarseness persists for more than 3 weeks, evaluation by an otorhinolaryngologist is recommended.
procedimientos.laringe.desc.3: Dr. Lumbán performs laryngoscopy to diagnose and treat voice disorders, allowing visualization of the vocal cords using a camera system.
procedimientos.laringe.desc.4: The evaluation begins with a complete medical history and detailed physical examination of the head and neck. Subsequently, the larynx is examined with a rigid or flexible fiber optic laryngoscope, with local anesthesia and minimal discomfort.
procedimientos.laringe.desc.5: During the study, the presence of inflammation, weakness, and lesions such as nodules, polyps, cysts, scars, hemorrhages, papillomas, and cancer are evaluated.
procedimientos.laringe.tratamiento.medic: Modification of voice use and lifestyle, Vocal hygiene, Voice rest, Vocal exercises
procedimientos.laringe.tratamiento.conju: Management is usually carried out jointly between the Otorhinolaryngologist and, in some cases, a Phoniatrist or Voice Therapist.
procedimientos.laringe.tratamiento.quiru: Removal of cysts, polyps, or nodules
Excision of pre-cancerous or cancerous lesions
procedimientos.laringe.cirugia.desc.1: Vocal cord surgery is performed by micro-laryngoscopy under general anesthesia. The patient remains completely asleep while the vocal cords are examined using a microscope.
procedimientos.laringe.cirugia.desc.2: High-precision microscopic instruments are used and, in some cases, a CO₂ laser to remove or treat the affected tissue.
procedimientos.laringe.postoperatorio: Most surgeries are outpatient, Limited voice rest after the procedure, Return to work approximately in 1 week, Progressive voice improvement over several weeks

septoplastia.titulo_completo: Septoplasty: Correction of the nasal septum to improve breathing
septoplastia.descripcion1: Correction of the nasal septum, known as septoplasty, is one of the most common procedures in otorhinolaryngology. The nasal septum is the wall of bone and cartilage that divides the two nostrils; when it is deviated — either from birth or due to trauma — it can obstruct the passage of air.
septoplastia.descripcion2: Having a deviated septum is common, but if it is too deviated, it can obstruct airflow. This makes breathing difficult through one or both sides of the nose.

anatomia.titulo: Anatomy of your nose: How does it work?
anatomia.descripcion: The nasal septum fulfills fundamental functions: it provides structural support to the nose and directs airflow in a balanced manner. The septum is made of thin bone in the back and cartilage in the front.
anatomia.nota: A crooked septum can make breathing difficult. It can also cause snoring and sleep apnea.

1.descripcion: Persistent difficulty breathing through one or both nostrils

3.descripcion: Constant sensation of dryness or irritation in the nose

4.descripcion: Changes in nasal mucus and frequent congestion

cirugia.titulo: Surgery: What does a septoplasty consist of?
cirugia.descripcion1: Septoplasty aims to correct the deformity of the septum or reconstruct it. Depending on the patient's needs, it can be performed alone or combined with rhinoplasty (cosmetic), turbinate surgery, or nasal valve surgery.
cirugia.descripcion2: During septoplasty, the septum is repositioned back to the center of the nose. To do this, Dr. Lumbán first reshapes, removes, or reinserts parts of the cartilage and bone in the correct position to clear the airways.

1.descripcion: Achieved through a small incision inside the nostril, leaving no visible scars.

2.descripcion: It is a procedure that usually takes less than an hour and does not require hospitalization.

3.descripcion: The vast majority of patients report minimal pain and can return to desk work within 3 to 5 days.

tecnica.descripcion: Dr. Lumbán does not use nasal packing that blocks airflow after surgery. This allows the patient to leave the hospital breathing without obstructions from the very first moment.

1.descripcion: Restores airflow, improving not only breathing but also sleep quality.

2.descripcion: Used as an auxiliary treatment in patients with sleep apnea, improving rest quality.

3.descripcion: Beneficial for athletes who need adequate airflow during physical activity.

4.descripcion: Patients who previously breathed through their mouth while sleeping now enjoy natural nasal breathing.

diferencias.septoplastia.desc: Focuses on the function of the nasal septum, correcting deviations to improve breathing.
diferencias.rinoplastia.desc: Deals with the aesthetics of the nose, modifying its shape and external appearance.

nota.desc: Occasionally, both procedures can be performed in combination to address both functional and aesthetic problems.

1.descripcion: It is normal to have slight swelling and congestion, which decrease noticeably by the end of the first week.

2.descripcion: Most patients return to their daily activities with basic precautions.

3.descripcion: Tissue usually feels completely restored between 4 and 6 weeks.

vertigo.subtitulo: Why do they occur and when to see a specialist?

descripcion.intro: Feeling that everything around you is moving or losing stability is one of the most frequent reasons for medical consultation with Dr. Lumbán. Understanding how the balance system works helps identify symptoms and seek consultation.

que-es.descripcion: Vertigo is a balance disorder characterized by a false sensation of movement, generally described as if everything were spinning around or as if the person were spinning.

sintomas.titulo: During episodes, the following may occur:

periferico.desc: It is the most frequent. It is due to an alteration in the labyrinth or the vestibular nerve. It usually includes auditory symptoms such as tinnitus or ear pressure.

central.desc: It originates from alterations in the brain or brainstem. Here instability is usually very marked and there may be double vision.

mareo.descripcion: Dizziness is the sensation of instability or 'empty head'. It may include imminent fainting, cold sweating, paleness, nausea, and general malaise. Unlike vertigo, dizziness does not always involve a spinning sensation, and may be related to circulatory, neurological, or metabolic problems.

equilibrio.titulo: How does our balance work? The role of the inner ear

descripcion.1: Balance does not depend on a single organ, but on several systems coordinated by the brain.

vestibular.desc: Located in the inner ear, it detects head movements and position.

visual.desc: The eyes provide information about the body's position in space.

propioceptivo.desc: Muscles and joints send signals about body position.

oido-interno.titulo: The inner ear and the vestibular system
oido-interno.descripcion: Inside the inner ear there is a structure called the labyrinth, made up of bone and soft tissues filled with fluid. This system detects head movements and body position.

conductos.desc: They are three fluid-filled tubes that detect head turns. Inside them, a gelatinous structure called the cupula acts like a 'ship's sail' that moves with the fluid.
conductos.proceso: When we move our head, the fluid moves, the cupula flexes, and sensory cells generate a nerve signal to the brain.

otolitos.desc: Between the semicircular canals and the cochlea are the utricle and saccule.
otolitos.funcion: These structures detect gravity. Thanks to them, the brain knows if you are sitting, lying down, or moving sideways.

causas.titulo: Frequent causes of vertigo and dizziness

enfermedades.titulo: Most common diseases related to vertigo

vppb.desc: Occurs when small calcium crystals (otoliths) detach and float in the ear canals, causing brief but intense vertigo when moving the head.

laberintitis.desc: Inflammation or infection of the inner ear, usually associated with viral respiratory infections. It can cause intense vertigo, loss of balance, and nausea.

meniere.desc: Characterized by recurrent episodes of vertigo, hearing loss, ear ringing (tinnitus), and feeling of ear fullness. It is related to alterations of the fluid inside the labyrinth.

fistula.desc: A fluid leak in the inner ear, common after trauma or sudden pressure changes.

perdida-audicion.titulo: Hearing Loss: Everything you need to know about your ears with an otorhinolaryngologist
perdida-audicion.subtitulo: Hearing loss is considered disabling when it exceeds 35 decibels (dB) in the ear with better hearing ability. This condition can range from mild to profound, affecting one or both ears, making it difficult to understand conversations or detect loud sounds.
perdida-audicion.subtitulo2: A key issue with hearing loss is that it is usually gradual. Because it develops slowly over the years, the patient often only becomes aware of the problem when it has already advanced significantly.

clasificacion.titulo: Classification and Types of Hearing Loss
clasificacion.subtitulo: The loss of hearing ability, also known as hypoacusis, is classified according to the area of the auditory system that is affected

conductiva.descripcion: Occurs when there is an obstacle that prevents sound from reaching the sensory structures of the inner ear. The problem can be located in the external auditory canal, eardrum, or middle ear.
conductiva.nota: It makes sounds seem muffled. This type of hearing loss can often be corrected through medical or surgical intervention.
lista: Fluid in the middle ear due to colds or allergies

neurosensorial.descripcion: This is the most common type of permanent hearing loss. It occurs when sound reaches the inner ear but cannot be translated into nerve impulses, or the nerve impulses are not transported to the brain.
neurosensorial.nota: It is generally not possible to repair through medical or surgical intervention.

mixta.descripcion: It is a combination of the two previous types. It can be caused by severe head trauma, chronic infection, or a genetic disorder.
mixta.ejemplo: An example of mixed hearing loss would be if a person who normally has sensorineural hearing loss suffered an ear infection.

causas.intro: In addition to the general types, there are specific conditions that Dr. Lumbán frequently evaluates:

cera.descripcion: Sometimes, wax accumulates in the ear canal and, in some cases, can completely block it. This often happens with hearing aid use, as the mold or housing tends to compress the wax into the ear canal, which can lead to plugs forming that substantially reduce hearing.

ruido.descripcion1: Exposure to extreme noise (such as a gunshot or nearby explosion) can cause sudden hearing loss, known as acoustic trauma. Hearing loss caused by acoustic trauma usually disappears within a day (unless the blast wave has also injured the eardrum or middle ear).
ruido.descripcion2: However, it is long-term exposure to noise that causes most noise-induced hearing loss.

infecciones.titulo: Ear infections (especially in children and young adults)
infecciones.otitis: Otitis and Cholesteatoma: Infections can be acute (from bacteria from the pharynx) or chronic (from eardrum perforation). Chronic otitis can lead to cholesteatoma, a mass of cells with benign tumor behavior that requires specialized attention.
infecciones.otosclerosis: Otosclerosis: It is a disease of the middle ear where bone growth around the stapes prevents the ossicles from vibrating correctly, making sound transmission difficult.

signos.titulo: How do I know if I'm losing my hearing?
signos.subtitulo: (Warning Signs) - If you or a family member experience the following signs, it's time to schedule a consultation with Dr. Lumbán:
lista: Difficulty understanding specific words during a conversation
Frequently asking people to repeat words
Avoiding social situations due to difficulty hearing others
Problems following conversations in groups or in the presence of background noise
Noises in the ear such as ringing, roaring, whistling, buzzing, etc.

grados.subtitulo: To measure severity, specialists use the decibel scale (dB HL)

congestion-nasal.subtitulo: Specialized treatment for stuffy nose and breathing problems
congestion-nasal.titulo_completo: Nasal Congestion: Specialized treatment for stuffy nose and breathing problems
congestion-nasal.descripcion1: Nasal congestion occurs when the inside of the nose swells due to inflamed blood vessels.
congestion-nasal.descripcion2: The problem may also include rhinorrhea or nasal discharge. If there is excess mucus dripping down the back of the throat (postnasal drip), it can cause cough or sore throat.
congestion-nasal.descripcion3: Untreated nasal congestion can lead to hearing problems, chronic fatigue, insomnia, headaches. It can also increase the frequency and volume of snoring, leading to Sleep Apnea.
congestion-nasal.desc: Nasal congestion occurs when the inside of the nose swells due to inflamed blood vessels. The problem may also include rhinorrhea or nasal discharge.
congestion-nasal.importante.desc: Untreated nasal congestion can lead to hearing problems, chronic fatigue, insomnia, headaches.

infecciones.viral: The flu or acute sinusitis secondary to a common cold are caused by a viral infection. These viruses are airborne and cause inflammation of nasal tissues.
infecciones.bacteriana: If the nasal mucosa turns yellow or green, it indicates that it has complicated with a bacterial infection. Sinus infection also causes nasal congestion, headaches, irritated throat, cough and general malaise.

anomalias.desc: Include nasal deformities, such as deviation of the nasal septum; these deformities may be secondary to injury or present from birth.
anomalias.otras: Other structural causes: hypertrophied turbinates, nasal polyps, nasal valve collapse, crooked nose and obstructive adenoids (common in children).

alergias.desc: They occur due to the inflammatory response to harmless environmental substances (allergens) such as pollen, dust mites, household dust, animal dander and tobacco smoke.
alergias.histamina: These allergens release a substance called histamine that can cause congestion and excessive nasal mucus production.

vasomotora.desc: It is a non-allergic condition that causes inflammation of the nasal membranes due to an abnormal reaction of the nerves that control the blood vessels of the nose.
vasomotora.factores: Triggering factors: temperature changes, humidity, strong odors such as air fresheners and cleaners, and tobacco smoke.

diagnostico.examen: Complete physical examination of nose and throat
diagnostico.sueno: Sleep pattern analysis in suspected apnea cases

medico.lavados: Nasal washes with saline solution 3 to 4 times a day

generales.humo: Do not smoke and avoid tobacco smoke

casa.lavados: Nasal washes with saline solution 3 to 4 times a day

prevencion.nota: Do not use topical decongestants for prolonged periods: patients who use decongestants for 3 to 5 days often experience rebound congestion when the drug effects wear off, leading them to continue use in a vicious cycle.

cta.mensaje: If you suffer from constant congestion and are interested in a treatment plan to relieve and recover your respiratory health, we invite you to schedule an evaluation with Dr. Lumbán, expert in nose, head and neck conditions in Tijuana.

obstruccion-nasal.subtitulo: Specialized solutions to improve your breathing
obstruccion-nasal.titulo_completo: Nasal Obstruction: Specialized solutions to improve your breathing
obstruccion-nasal.descripcion1: Nasal obstruction is a frequent symptom derived from various conditions that block, totally or partially, the airways.
obstruccion-nasal.descripcion2: This condition manifests as if something were restricting the airflow to breathe easily.

tabique.desc: The septum is the structure of bone and cartilage that divides the nose into two cavities. If it is crooked, it generates a fixed mechanical obstruction.
tabique.fijo: Deviated septum: fixed mechanical obstruction that does not respond to medication

cornetes.desc: The inferior turbinates can excessively enlarge due to allergies or irritants.
cornetes.mejora: Turbinate hypertrophy: medical treatment helps, but in severe cases surgery is required

adenoides.desc: They are glands located behind the nasal cavity. When inflamed, they narrow the respiratory passage, being the main cause of obstruction in children (although rare in adults).

rinitis.desc: Infections or allergies can inflame internal tissues. Conditions such as allergic rhinitis, vasomotor rhinitis, sinusitis, and nasal vestibulitis significantly restrict airflow.

tabique.desc: The septum is the structure of bone and cartilage that divides the nose into two cavities. If it is crooked, it generates a fixed mechanical obstruction that does not respond to medication.
tabique.solucion: In these cases, the only definitive solution is septoplasty.

polipos.desc: They are soft, non-cancerous growths on the lining of the nasal passages or sinuses that act as a physical barrier to air.

cornetes.desc: The inferior turbinates can excessively enlarge due to allergies or irritants. Although medical treatment helps, in severe cases surgical reduction is required.

valvula.desc: The nasal valve is the narrowest area of the airway. If its walls are weak and collapse when inhaling, breathing becomes difficult.

coanas.desc: A congenital condition where babies are born with excess tissue that obstructs the nasal passages, requiring immediate attention.

quirurgico.endoscopica: Nasal endoscopic surgery: To remove polyps or treat chronic sinusitis

garganta.desc: Learn about conditions related to the throat

desc.1: The throat or pharynx is a tubular structure that connects the oral and nasal cavities with the esophagus and larynx (voice box). Food passes to the esophagus and air to the trachea and larynx.
desc.2: Being a common passage for food and air, it is more susceptible to infections and other conditions. Dr. Lumbán offers expert diagnosis and specialized treatment for multiple throat conditions.

amigdalitis.desc: Inflammation of the tonsils caused by viruses or bacteria. They are part of the lymphatic system and help prevent infections.
amigdalitis.sintomas: Difficulty swallowing, Nausea and vomiting, Redness of tonsils

tratamiento.medico: Ibuprofen or acetaminophen, Antibiotics (penicillin), Plenty of fluids, Salt water gargles
tratamiento.quirurgico: Tonsillectomy in recurrent, persistent, or severe cases.

dolor.desc: It is the most common throat disorder. Generally caused by cold, flu, allergies, bacteria (streptococcus), smoking, tonsillitis, or infectious mononucleosis.
dolor.tratamiento: Lozenges and candies, Salt water gargles, Antibiotics if recurrent

faringitis.desc: Inflammation of the pharynx caused by viruses or bacteria. Main symptom: sore throat; other symptoms: fever, headache, muscle and joint pain, rashes, and swollen lymph nodes.

cancer.desc: Tumors in the pharynx, larynx, or tonsils. Main risk factor: tobacco use.
cancer.riesgos: Tobacco use (smoked and smokeless), Chronic alcoholism, Human papillomavirus, Betel nut chewing, Exposure to ultraviolet light
cancer.sintomas: Lump that does not heal, Persistent sore throat, Hoarseness or voice changes
cancer.diagnostico: Diagnosis: biopsy, specialized tests, and complete evaluation.
cancer.tratamiento: Radiotherapy for specific cases, Surgery: Partial or total laryngectomy, Combination: radiation and chemotherapy for large tumors
cancer.rehabilitacion: After a laryngectomy, activities such as eating, speaking, or breathing can be difficult. Speech and swallowing therapy is recommended.

cta.desc: Dr. Lumbán offers expert diagnosis and specialized treatment for throat conditions.

desc.1: Sleep apnea is a common disorder where patients have abnormal breathing patterns during sleep, including breathing pauses or very shallow breathing. These pauses last between 10 and 20 seconds or more, interrupting sleep and reducing blood oxygen levels.
desc.2: Obstructive sleep apnea can increase with age and is more common in men, overweight people, and those with heart disease. If left untreated, it can lead to hypertension, heart failure, heart rhythm disturbances, insulin resistance, and even death.

central.desc: Occurs when signals from the brain to the respiratory muscles are interrupted, and there is no effort from the breathing muscles.

obstructiva.desc: It is the most common type and occurs due to an obstruction in the airway that prevents adequate airflow. Brain signals are not interrupted, but muscular efforts are not sufficient.

mixta.desc: Combination of central and obstructive apnea, presenting both mechanisms of respiratory interruption.

comportamiento.peso: Weight loss in case of overweight

dentales.desc: Devices that keep the jaw forward, useful for mild apnea or in those who do not respond to behavioral changes.

nasales.tiras: Adhesive nasal strips to widen nostrils

cpap.desc: CPAP prevents airway narrowing during breathing, maintaining constant airflow and persistent pressure.

desc.1: The voice is the sound produced when air passes from the lungs to the larynx. When speaking, the vocal cords partially close, causing the air to vibrate and generate sound. Each voice is as unique as a fingerprint.
desc.2: Various medical conditions or damage to the parts associated with the voice can cause pain, discomfort, changes in pitch, volume, or voice quality.

nodulos.desc: Non-cancerous growths on the vocal cords caused by overuse.

polipos.desc: Swelling or abnormal nodule on one or both vocal cords.

paralisis.desc: Occurs when one or both vocal cords do not move correctly, affecting voice, swallowing, and breathing.

paradójico.desc: Dysfunction where the vocal cords close when inhaling instead of opening, causing breathing problems.

disfonia.desc: Chronic disorder caused by forced or tense movements of the vocal cords, producing abnormal voice changes.

causas.principales: Vocal cord injury, Overuse of voice, Talking too much or shouting, Smoking
causas.otras: Common cold, Bronchitis, Exposure to irritating substances

voz.sintomas: Hoarse or rough voice, Abnormal voice changes, Difficulty breathing, Persistent cough, Feeling of a lump in the throat

diagnostico.historia: Evaluation of symptoms, vocal habits, and medical history
diagnostico.examen: Visual evaluation of the larynx and vocal cords
diagnostico.pruebas: Evaluation of vocal cord vibration and laryngeal function

voz.profesionales: For voice professionals (teachers, singers, broadcasters, etc.), early attention to any voice change is crucial to prevent permanent damage.

pediatrico.desc: Learn about different ear, nose, and throat diseases in children
pediatrico.intro: Children and adolescents should not be confused with adults for the diagnosis and treatment of Ear, Nose, and Throat diseases. Height, weight, immune system, and physical/mental development require special care.

sinusitis.titulo: How can I tell if my child has sinusitis?
sinusitis.desc: Sinusitis in children is different from sinusitis in adults. The following symptoms may indicate a sinus infection in your child:
sinusitis.sintomas: Chills lasting 10 to 14 days or low to moderate fever., Thick, yellow-green mucus., Post-nasal drip, sometimes manifested as sore throat, cough, bad breath, and/or vomiting., Headache, usually in children 6 years or older., Irritability., Low energy., Swelling around the eyes.
sinusitis.explicacion: Young children have immature immune systems and are more prone to infections of the nose, sinuses, and ears, especially in the first years of life. These are most often caused by viral infections (colds) and can be aggravated by allergies. However, when your child remains sick beyond the usual seven to ten days, they likely have an infection called sinusitis.
sinusitis.reducir-riesgo: You can reduce your child's risk of nose infections by reducing exposure to known environmental allergies and pollutants such as tobacco smoke, reducing time in daycare, and treating stomach acid reflux disease.

ronquidos.titulo: When snoring isn't so cute. Children and sleep apnea

desc.1: It is often cute when children try to imitate their parents. However, when it comes to snoring, it's no laughing matter and is abnormal in children. In reality, children are not just smaller versions of adults, and snoring usually indicates a more serious underlying problem, such as obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
desc.2: During the deepest stages of sleep, muscles relax allowing the tonsils to shift inward. In children with enlarged tonsils, this blocks breathing and causes interrupted sleep, resulting in daytime exhaustion.
desc.3: Recent studies have shown that school performance is significantly affected, with attention disorders and behavioral problems more evident in children with OSA. Even the best students suffer without a good night's rest.

ronquidos.solucion: The solution begins with an accurate sleep history. Children who snore should be evaluated by an otorhinolaryngologist, especially if they have enlarged tonsils. If OSA is diagnosed, removal of tonsils and adenoids is the first line of treatment. Techniques such as radiofrequency allow rapid recovery and improve sleep quality and growth.

desc.1: Ventilation tubes are small cylinders, 1mm in diameter, placed through the eardrum (tympanic membrane) to allow air to enter the middle ear. They are also called tympanostomy, myringotomy, or decompression tubes. They can be plastic, metal, or teflon, and some have a coating to reduce the possibility of infection.
desc.2: There are two basic types of tubes: short-term (stay in 6 to 12 months before falling out on their own) and long-term (larger, with flanges that hold them in place longer, usually requiring removal by an otorhinolaryngologist).

desc.1: They are recommended when a child experiences repeated middle ear infections (acute otitis media) or hearing loss due to persistent fluid (otitis media with effusion). This can affect speech, balance, and hearing.
desc.2: They are also indicated in cases of eardrum or Eustachian tube malformations, Down Syndrome, cleft palate, or barotrauma. Each year, over half a million ear tube surgeries are performed in children (the most common childhood surgery), with an average age of 1 to 3 years.

quien.beneficios: Tubes restore hearing, reduce risk of future infections, improve behavior, sleep, speech, and balance.

insercion.desc: Insertion is performed through myringotomy, an outpatient surgical procedure consisting of a 1-2 mm incision in the eardrum. It is performed under a surgical microscope or laser. The tube is placed to keep the hole open and allow ventilation of the middle ear.
insercion.procedimiento: Light general anesthesia (laughing gas) is administered in young children; some older children may tolerate without anesthesia. Myringotomy is performed, fluid is suctioned from the middle ear, and the ventilation tube is placed. The procedure lasts less than 15 minutes.
insercion.adenoides: In some cases, removal of adenoid tissue is recommended simultaneously to reduce the risk of recurrent infections.

expectativas.titulo: What to expect after this surgery?

desc.1: After surgery, patients are monitored in recovery and usually go home within a few hours. There may be drowsiness, irritability, or nausea from anesthesia. Hearing is restored immediately and normal sounds may seem very loud.
desc.2: Specific postoperative instructions are provided, including when to seek immediate attention. To avoid bacteria, it may be recommended to keep ears dry using plugs during bathing or swimming. In activities such as diving or dirty water, protection is necessary; consult your doctor.

ronquidos.datos.interesantes.1: One in four people have chronic snoring that they cannot stop on their own.
ronquidos.datos.interesantes.2: Chronic snoring can strain relationships with bed partners.
ronquidos.datos.interesantes.3: On average, the partner of a snoring person loses one hour of sleep each night.
ronquidos.datos.interesantes.5: Snoring can indicate a more serious problem: obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
ronquidos.datos.interesantes.6: It can be improved or eliminated in most people with simple in-office procedures.

causas.desc: During sleep, the body's muscles, including those in the throat, relax. This can cause flaccid or excessive tissue to vibrate as air passes through, producing snoring. The affected areas include the nose, soft palate, uvula, and/or tonsils. Dr. Lumbán will work with you to determine the exact cause and the most appropriate treatment.
